subsystems.name: Production strain
subsystems.role: the engineered microbe that actually makes the protein.
parts: gene construct with a strong promoter

subsystems.name: Seed train
subsystems.role: grows a tiny vial of cells into enough biomass to inoculate a production vessel.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: the controlled vessel where the cells grow and secrete protein.

subsystems.name: Media and sterilisation
subsystems.role: feeds the cells without letting contaminants in.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: separates the protein from cells, water and spent broth.

subsystems.name: Urban utilities and containment
subsystems.role: lets the plant sit inside a city without waste or release problems.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the strain
buildSteps.detail: Genes for the target protein are inserted into a food-safe host such as a yeast, with a promoter that switches production on and a signal that pushes the protein out of the cell.

buildSteps.title: Bank and test the cells
buildSteps.detail: A single validated colony is frozen into working cell banks so every production run starts from the same genetics.

buildSteps.title: Grow the seed train
buildSteps.detail: The culture is stepped up from millilitre flasks to a pilot vessel and then to the production fermenter, each step a roughly tenfold increase in volume.

buildSteps.title: Build the fermentation suite
buildSteps.detail: The vessel, agitator, sterile piping, steam supply and control system are installed — in cities, usually inside an existing industrial or food-processing building with road and rail access.

buildSteps.title: Sterilise and charge the medium
buildSteps.detail: Media is heat-sterilised and pumped in; the vessel is steamed before inoculation to keep competing microbes out.

buildSteps.title: Run the fed-batch fermentation
buildSteps.detail: The culture is held near 30 °C with controlled pH, oxygen and a gradual sugar feed for several days — the protein accumulates in the broth.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and separate
buildSteps.detail: The broth is chilled and centrifuged or filtered to remove cells and debris.

buildSteps.title: Purify and dry
buildSteps.detail: Chromatography and membrane steps isolate the protein, which is concentrated and dried into a stable powder.

buildSteps.title: Formulate and distribute
buildSteps.detail: The powder becomes food ingredients, and spent broth, waste heat and water go to digestion, district heating or on-site reuse rather than to sewer.

prerequisites.why: without a reliably high-yielding engineered host, the economics never work.
antibiotics, enzymes and citric acid have been made this way for decades; the skill base is mature.
sugar, cooling and aeration dominate running cost, so cheap clean power and feedstock decide viability.
each new protein needs food-safety clearance, and pathways differ by country.
separation and drying often cost more than the fermentation itself, which is what blocks commodity pricing.

pathway.milestone: precision fermentation already supplies high-value ingredients such as cheese rennet, insulin, and animal-identical whey and egg proteins from vessels of tens to hundreds of cubic metres
pathway.unlocks: a proven technical base and a trained workforce.

pathway.milestone: larger plants producing commodity dairy and egg proteins at or near price parity
pathway.unlocks: substitution of bulk livestock protein rather than niche ingredients.

pathway.milestone: city plants co-located with food-waste digestion, using waste heat and urban carbon sources as feedstock
pathway.unlocks: short supply chains and less freight for perishable protein.

pathway.milestone: a measurable share of a city's protein made locally in bioreactor districts
pathway.unlocks: lower land, water and emissions per kilogram of protein, and more resilience to import disruption.
